**RE: Member appeal of adverse benefit determination dated 2026-08-17**

- **Member name:** Quinn Delgado
- **Member ID:** W570305899
- **Reference number:** POC-A389519C6D-33639
- **Plan / product:** Avera Health Plans, Commercial/ACA (South Dakota)
- **Service denied:** Bunion surgery (hallux valgus), CPT 28296
- **Governing policy:** *Cohere Medical Policy – Great Toe Surgical Treatments (Version 3), Avera Health Plans* — https://help.coherehealth.com/payer-info/en/articles/13602157-avera-health-plan-commercial-guidelines#great-toe-surgical-treatments-v3

---

To the Appeals Reviewer:

I am appealing the denial of coverage for my bunion surgery (CPT 28296), which Avera Health Plans denied on 2026-08-17 on the grounds that the procedure does not meet the plan's criteria for medical necessity. I am asking the plan to reconsider that decision. I am writing about the criteria in the policy named above, and below I line up the plan's own published language against what my medical records actually say. My surgeon, Dr. Marchetti, MD (orthopedic surgery), has documented that this procedure is needed.

## The plan's criteria and what my records show

**1. Length and content of conservative treatment.** The policy states:

> "Failure of conservative management for greater than 3 months, including ALL of the following"

My records document a course of conservative care well beyond three months. I have had 18 months of progressive pain in the foot, unrelieved by rest. I took NSAIDs for eight months with inadequate relief. I completed 20 visits of activity modification, wide toe-box footwear and a custom orthotic over 12 weeks, from 2026-04-02 to 2026-06-25, documented in the physical therapy discharge note. I also had a corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-04, which gave only three weeks of partial relief.

Within that requirement, the policy lists as one component:

> "Oral steroids, topical or oral anti-inflammatory medications, or oral analgesics"

This is documented: eight months of NSAIDs with inadequate relief.

The policy also lists:

> "Taping or splinting; OR Toe spacer; OR Toe sleeve; OR Padding"

My records document activity modification, wide toe-box footwear and a custom orthotic. If the plan's position is that one of the specific items in this list is missing from the chart, I ask the plan to say so in writing and identify it, so that my surgeon can supply the documentation or explain what was used instead. I would note that the excerpt above introduces a list, and the policy text I have been able to obtain does not reproduce every element the plan may have applied.

**2. Skeletal maturity.** The policy states:

> "Documentation of near or full skeletal maturity as indicated by first metatarsal physeal closure or near closure"

My records as summarized do not include a statement on physeal closure. My treating surgeon can confirm this finding: [surgeon's statement regarding first metatarsal physeal closure or near closure]. If this was the basis for the denial, I ask that the plan identify it plainly so it can be addressed with a single note from my surgeon rather than a full denial of surgery.

**3. Connective tissue or neuromuscular disorders.** The policy states:

> "Documentation of connective tissue or neuromuscular disorders that may affect etiology or severity of the condition (e.g., Cerebral Palsy, Ehlers-Danlos Syndrome, Marfan Syndrome, Osteogenesis Imperfecta, Fibrodysplasia Ossificans Progressiva)"

My records do not contain any such diagnosis. [If applicable, surgeon to confirm presence or absence of any connective tissue or neuromuscular disorder.]

**4. Procedure type.** The policy states:

> "The procedure is a bunionectomy with osteotomy, and ALL of the following"

The procedure my surgeon requested is CPT 28296, as identified in the plan's own denial notice. This excerpt ends in a colon and introduces further conditions that are not reproduced in the policy text available to me; I ask the plan to identify each condition it applied under this heading.

**5. Nicotine use.** The policy states:

> "Current nicotine user with no product use for 6 weeks; and ANY of the following"

and lists, among the alternatives:

> "Negative urine (cotinine) lab test within 30 days"

> "Surgery is urgently required due to documented reason"

> "No history of nicotine product use within the last 12 months"

> "No lifetime history of nicotine product use"

My records state that I am a non-smoker. My records also document no active infection and no untreated substance use, with a BMI of 29. If the plan requires a specific confirmation under this heading — for example a cotinine test or a statement about lifetime use — I ask the plan to identify which one it applied, and my surgeon can provide it: [surgeon or lab documentation of nicotine status, if required].

**6. Positive findings.** The policy states:

> "The patient has ANY of the following positive findings"

and includes:

> "Pain, swelling, or limited range of motion (ROM) at the first metatarsophalangeal (MTP) joint"

My examination documents positive provocative testing on the affected side and range of motion limited by pain. I also cannot tolerate closed shoes, and my records note ulceration risk over the prominence. Because the policy requires only **any** one of the listed findings, the documented pain and limited range of motion satisfy this criterion on its own.

**7. Radiographic confirmation.** The policy states:

> "Radiographic confirmation with radiologic report (must be weight-bearing radiographs of the foot) of ALL of the following"

and:

> "HV angle greater than 15°; OR IM angle greater than 9°"

My imaging from 2026-06-07 consists of weight-bearing foot radiographs showing a hallux valgus angle of 38 degrees and an intermetatarsal angle of 17 degrees. Both measurements exceed both of the thresholds the plan has published, so this criterion is met on either reading of the excerpt.

## Request for the criteria the plan actually applied

I am asking Avera Health Plans, in writing, for the exact clinical criteria used to deny this request, including the name and edition of any review guideline relied upon, the specific criterion or criteria the plan found unmet, and the credentials of the reviewer who made the determination. I understand I am entitled to this information. The plan holds the criteria it applied; I do not. The denial notice states only that the request does not meet the plan's criteria for medical necessity, without identifying which criterion was not satisfied, and I cannot fully respond to a reason I have not been given.

I also want to be transparent about one point: the policy excerpts quoted above are the only policy language I have. Several of them end in a colon and introduce lists of further conditions that are not reproduced in what I was able to obtain. Where I could not quote the plan, I have argued from what my records state rather than guessing at a threshold, and I have not attributed any requirement to the plan that I could not quote word for word.

## What I am asking for

I ask that this denial be overturned and that CPT 28296 be authorized. I ask that the reviewer read the physical therapy discharge note dated through 2026-06-25, the weight-bearing radiology report dated 2026-06-07, the record of eight months of NSAID use, and the 2026-05-04 injection note alongside the policy criteria quoted above. If any single item of documentation is still considered missing, I ask that the plan identify it specifically so my surgeon and I can provide it, rather than denying the surgery outright.

I am submitting this appeal within the timeframe stated in the plan's notice. The notice states my appeal must be received within 180 days of 2026-08-17, that is, by **2027-02-13**. I am sending it to the appeal address printed on my denial letter; any member who is unsure where to file can call the number on the back of the insurance card and ask where member appeals are filed.

Please confirm in writing that you have received this appeal, and please send the determination and the requested criteria to me at the address above. I am glad to supply any additional records you need, and my surgeon's office can be reached at [surgeon's office phone].

Thank you for reviewing this again.

Sincerely,

_______________________________
**Quinn Delgado**

Reference number: POC-A389519C6D-33639
